finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: The name field is populated with attacker-controlled data and is directly passed to the printf function.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the printf call at line 71 uses a compile‑time constant format string "Record %d: %s %s\n"; the untrusted data (chunk.records[i].name) is passed as an argument, not as part of the format string, so it cannot be interpreted as a format specifier or command. No control flow from the source reaches the sink without the safe format. No other checks are needed.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.assumptions: The name field is populated with attacker-controlled data and is stored in a 15-character buffer.

parsed.refutation_attempt: I inspected the fragment for any statements that write into the `name` buffer of `struct Record`. No assignment, `strcpy`, `scanf`, or other input‑related function is present in the provided code that could supply attacker‑controlled data to `chunk.records[i].name`. The only operations on the buffer are reads performed by `strcmp` during sorting. Since the source of untrusted data is absent, there is no feasible path from attacker input to the `name[15]` sink in this fragment.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.assumptions: The surname field is populated with attacker-controlled data and is stored in a 25-character buffer.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked for size/range validations before copying to surname, but no such code is present in the fragment. Searched for constant arguments in copy functions and for unreachable paths; none found. Since the fragment omits the code that populates the surname field, the claim depends on unseen code.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.assumptions: The address field is populated with attacker-controlled data and is stored in a 50-character buffer.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Searched for any assignment, copy, or input handling that writes to chunk.records[i].address. No such code exists in the fragment. The struct definition (lines 6-8) only declares the array; no function populates it. Therefore there is no path from an untrusted source to the sink address[50].
